DiffTRe avoids differentiating through the MD simulation. It combines automatic differentiation with MD reweighting schemes and leverages thermodynamic perturbation theory, which is limited to time-independent observables [W3168247670#001][W3168247670#003]. Direct reverse-mode AD instead backpropagates through the whole trajectory, which is memory-hungry and prone to exploding gradients [W3168247670#003][W3168247670#011]. DiffTRe only differentiates through the potential energy computation of decorrelated states [W3168247670#011].

This yields gradient computation about 2 orders of magnitude faster, with exploding gradients avoided and memory requirements comparable to the adjoint method [W3168247670#001][W3168247670#003]. In the toy double-well example, the authors measured a gradient speed-up of 486 and an overall per-update speed-up of 3.7, though they note these values are sensitive to the setup [W3168247670#011]. Because the method is reweighting-based, dynamical properties cannot be used as target observables [W3168247670#019].
